notes: v287 + native v62 (1.35 / versionCode 37) — REWORK of the v61/286 ship (owner verdict Oct 30, 2026 13:31 MDT: 'Neither fixed and it messed up my Live km's while reinstall! Not fixed but worst!'). Three named items. (1) REINSTALL-LIVE-KM (NEW — the harm): reinstalling mid-shift broke live km on the running day. Three proven defects: D1 — ShiftTrack.sessionStarted was called only from the two start flows, never from a restore path, so after a reinstall the native foreground service + 45s crumb drain were never re-armed for the restored session and the rest of the shift's background miles went unrecorded; fix: ShiftTrack.sessionRestored(key), called from all three restore sites (init restore, App.onAuth reattach, first-pull callback). D3 — LiveMiles.startDay adopted same-day fragments only when no saved record existed; the cloud-restored session record orphaned the miles the fresh boot counted into the day-watch fragment before sign-in; fix: fragments now fold into the restored session too (mergeCrumbs timestamp dedupe keeps it exactly-once; folded fragment keys retire). D2 — a reinstall resets the location grant; the geo error latched the miles watcher broken and the banner's Allow flow never re-poked it; fix: a landed background grant (banner Allow + requestBackground) now calls LiveMiles.onVisible(). Plus: the APK's bundled www was web 234 (52 versions stale, predating the v222/v224 restore protections) and serves first on a fresh install — v62's bundled www is re-synced to web 287. (2) WIDGET-FREEZE (v61 FAILED in his hands): the exact-alarm chain silently degrades to inexact alarms when the exact-alarm grant is absent (a fresh install resets it) and Doze defers it; and the widget's miles came only from web-pushed strings — the session record carried no miles. Fix: (a) ShiftTrackingService, already awake for every GPS fix while recording, now repaints the widget from the record on a ~30s Handler tick (no grant needed; the alarm chain stays as backstop); (b) SessionRecord carries a WEB-SYNCED milesM (from LiveMiles' persisted record via sessionFacts — never natively derived), and the widget composes its miles line from the record on every paint (refreshFromRecord + buildViews). Honest residual: while the app process is fully dead, miles are as fresh as the web's last fold/sync; timer/loads/status stay live from the record. (3) PIP-HOME (v61 FAILED in his hands): the v286 harness had driven the module's back() directly with a mocked shell; the full chain has home-bound fallthroughs (any shell path that heads home without the module's back being consumed) that tore the module down — drive killed, no float. Fix: teardownModule (the choke point every home-bound path crosses) now asks the module to parkForHome() first — a live unparked drive parks and floats instead of dying; navigator.back() checks a live drive FIRST (before the face-flag staircase); the session-case park re-asserts the floated face once the dashboard landing settles. The v286/v227 behavior on the consumed-Back path is unchanged (proven by the same cases in the new harness). HARNESS: new tools/rework-v287-test.js 27/27 — RED on the v61/286 tree for every failure mode (restore rearm absent; fragment orphaned at 1.00 km vs 1.56 folded; no grant poke; no service tick / record miles; home-bound fallthrough kills the drive), GREEN after. It drives the REAL shifttrack.js, miles.js, navigator module and the REAL app.js SYS-BACK + shell slices end-to-end.
